seoTitle: Base64 Encoder / Decoder - Free Online Tool to Encode & Decode Text
metaDescription: Free online Base64 Encode and Decode tool. Instantly translate plain text or binary data into Base64 format, or decode a Base64 string back to readable text. No installation required.
intro: Need to safely transmit binary data over a text-only medium, embed images directly in CSS, or decode an authentication header? Base64 encoding is the standard solution used by web developers and system administrators every day. Our free online Base64 Encoder/Decoder provides instant, client-side translation between plain text and Base64 strings — no uploads, no server calls, and no installation required. Simply paste your data, select Encode or Decode, and get your result in milliseconds.
whatIs: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that represents binary data using only 64 printable ASCII characters (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, +, and /). Because many systems — including email, JSON, HTML, and URLs — are designed to handle text rather than raw binary data, Base64 acts as a universal adapter. It ensures that complex data remains intact and unmodified during transit across different systems and protocols. Our Base64 Encode/Decode tool is a developer utility that automates this translation process instantly in your browser.
howToUse: Select your desired action: 'Encode to Base64' or 'Decode to Text'.
Paste your text, binary data, or existing Base64 string into the input box.
The translated string will instantly appear in the output box.
Click the copy button to copy the result for use in your code or application.
howItWorks: Base64 encoding works by taking 3 bytes of raw data (24 bits) and splitting them into 4 chunks of 6 bits each. Each 6-bit chunk maps to one of the 64 safe ASCII characters. If the input data does not divide evenly into 3-byte groups, one or two '=' padding characters are appended to the output. Decoding reverses this exact mathematical process, reconstructing the original bytes from the Base64 character sequence. The entire operation runs locally in your browser using JavaScript's native btoa() and atob() functions.
workedExample: Encoding the word 'Hello'. The ASCII bytes for H, e, l, l, o are 72, 101, 108, 108, 111. Grouped into 3-byte chunks: [72, 101, 108] and [108, 111]. The first chunk (01001000 01100101 01101100) splits into four 6-bit values: 18, 6, 21, 44, which map to 'S', 'G', 'V', 's'. The second chunk maps to 'b', 'G', '8'. Appending one '=' pad gives the final result: 'SGVsbG8='.
resultInterpretation: The encoded output is a safe string of letters and numbers that will not trigger formatting errors in HTML, URLs, XML, or JSON files. It is safe to store in a database or transmit in an HTTP header. The decoded output is your original, human-readable text or binary data.
useCases: Web Development: Embedding small SVG icons or images directly into a CSS or HTML file using Data URIs, eliminating extra HTTP requests and speeding up page loads.
API & Authentication: Decoding HTTP Basic Authentication headers (transmitted as 'Base64(username:password)') to verify credentials in API integrations.
Email Protocols: MIME-encoded emails use Base64 to encode attachments and non-ASCII message bodies. Developers use decoders to inspect raw email content.
Data Storage: Storing binary data (like images or files) in text-only systems such as JSON configuration files or XML documents.
JWT Inspection: JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) use Base64URL encoding for their header and payload segments, making this tool useful for decoding and inspecting token contents.
tipsAndLimitations: Base64 is NOT encryption. It provides zero security. Anyone can decode a Base64 string instantly. Never use it to hide passwords or sensitive data without applying real encryption first.
Encoding data to Base64 increases its size by approximately 33%, which is a trade-off to be aware of when embedding large files.
This tool uses standard Base64 (RFC 4648). If you need Base64URL (used in JWTs), note that it replaces '+' with '-' and '/' with '_', and omits padding.
For very large files (megabytes of data), browser-based encoding may be slow. Use a server-side or command-line tool for bulk processing.

faq.question: Why does my Base64 string end with '='?
faq.answer: The equals sign (=) is used for padding. Base64 groups input data into 3-byte blocks. If the last block has only 1 byte, two '==' characters are added; if it has 2 bytes, one '=' is added. This padding ensures the output length is always a multiple of 4 characters.

faq.question: Is Base64 the same as encryption?
faq.answer: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not an encryption algorithm. Anyone who receives a Base64 string can decode it instantly without any key or password. It is designed for data compatibility, not data security.

faq.question: What is the difference between Base64 and Base64URL?
faq.answer: Standard Base64 uses '+' and '/' characters, which have special meaning in URLs and must be percent-encoded. Base64URL (used in JWTs and modern APIs) replaces '+' with '-' and '/' with '_', making it safe to use directly in URLs and HTTP headers without escaping.

faq.question: Can I encode images with this tool?
faq.answer: This tool encodes and decodes text strings. To embed an image, you would need to first read the image file as binary data. Most code editors and developer tools can generate Base64 Data URIs from image files directly. The encoded string from those tools can then be pasted into CSS as 'url(data:image/png;base64,...)'

faq.question: Why does my decoded output look like garbled characters?
faq.answer: This usually means you are trying to decode a string that is not valid Base64, or you are decoding the raw bytes of a binary file (like a PDF or image) as text. Text-based decoding only works correctly if the original data was plain text before it was encoded.

faq.question: Does this tool send my data to a server?
faq.answer: No. All encoding and decoding is performed entirely within your browser using JavaScript's native btoa() and atob() functions. Your input data is never transmitted to any server, making it completely private.
